key_insight: Fault-tolerant quantum computing needs compiler stacks that are code-aware, hardware-aware, and decoder-integrated rather than only circuit-optimizing.
engineering_relevance: This survey gives FTQC designers a roadmap for building end-to-end compilers that coordinate logical operations, syndrome extraction, and real-time decoding across diverse hardware platforms.
method: Organize the stack into logical-level QEC compilation, physical-level QEC realization, and decoder runtime integration.
Review lattice-surgery, code-surgery, magic-state distillation, and code-switching methods for implementing logical and non-Clifford operations.
Compare hardware-aware realization approaches on superconducting, trapped-ion, and neutral-atom systems.
evidence_signal: The paper is a survey synthesized from existing literature and frames its contribution as a full-stack organization of compiler and runtime methods rather than a new experimental benchmark.
watch_item: A major implementation challenge is cross-layer co-design, especially integrating qLDPC compilation, decoder latency, and runtime adaptivity into one benchmarkable FTQC stack.
paper_title: Quantum Compiler Design for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing
